facts.fact: 接下来一周她几次想打给 Claude，却总被拦住——像有件事先要办完她才敢认真对待两人的关系（也许这正是河边那天她说的意思）。
facts.anchor: Over the next week I picked up the phone to call Claude a few times, but something kept holding me back, like there was business I needed to take care of first, before I could take us seriously.

facts.fact: 万圣节店里忙：人们想要穿得像我朋友们穿的样子——但作为戏服；五个女孩要扮 Apollonia，她卖了五件蕾丝紧身衣。
facts.anchor: The store was busy because it was Halloween and people wanted to wear the things my friends wore, but as a costume.

facts.fact: Cynthia 在上州待了近两个月后回来；她表现良好、格外卖力，想让 Cynthia 卖店时多想想。
facts.anchor: She was back from almost two months upstate, and I was on good behavior, hustling a little more so maybe she’d think twice about selling the store.

facts.fact: 开门是 Rick：「你好，Bronstein 小姐。我为 Manhattan Remediation 工作。我想你用我们的服务。」
facts.anchor: “Hello, Miss Bronstein. I work for Manhattan Remediation. I believe you’ve used our services before.”

facts.fact: 像一直在等他上门：见他时升起的怒火也把她拉近——也许她喜欢这份愤怒，因为它「让一个系统有了一张脸」。
facts.anchor: It was like I had been waiting for him to show up. The anger that rose in me when I saw Rick’s face—it also drew me closer. Maybe I even liked the anger he provoked, because it put a face to a system.

facts.fact: 他在屋里四处打量（手指划过书脊、看 Kurt 拍的褪色宝丽来）；像一只因为感知到珍贵就打翻摆件的猫。
facts.anchor: He reminded me of a cat that might knock over a trinket because it could sense it was precious.

facts.fact: 《Ghost Town》之争：他说这首歌像是在论证「城镇变成鬼城不好」。（她回：他们大概不共享你的政治。）
facts.anchor: “Why not? It sounds like they’re arguing that it’s not good for your town to become a ghost town.”

facts.fact: Rick：我来告诉你，你做什么都威胁不到我们——我们用的是取之不尽的资源。
facts.anchor: “I’m here to explain to you that nothing you can do will threaten us. We’re working with an unlimited resource.”

facts.fact: 他翻她的速写本后停住，转身问：你认识 Mark Johansen？
facts.anchor: He turned back to me. “You know Mark Johansen?”

facts.fact: 像鞭子抽响：她没料到这一问，怀疑是否见血。
facts.anchor: It was like the flick of a whip. I didn’t see it coming and wondered if it drew a drop of blood.

facts.fact: Rick 说两人同校、同在田径队；他说 Mark 跑姿完美，「像漂在地上」。她承认这是真的——有人这样记得他，即使是 Rick。
facts.anchor: “We went to the same college; we were on the track team. Mark had perfect form when he ran. It was like he was floating above the ground.”

facts.fact: 她按 Mark 教的方式双手像短打般握起门口的球棒（以防被抢），命 Rick 滚出去。
facts.anchor: “Get the fuck out of my home.”

facts.fact: Rick 威胁：别以为你们在店面和我们仓库的胡闹改变了什么——放手吧。
facts.anchor: “Don’t think that your bullshit in our storefront or your rescue mission in the warehouse made any difference to what we’re doing. Just drop it.”

facts.fact: 她把球棒砸穿卧室门，想象那是 Rick、Silverman、Mark 的母亲、让 Mark 死的急诊医生们。
facts.anchor: So I put it through my bedroom door and pretended it was Rick, Silverman, Mark’s mother, the ER doctors who let him die.

facts.fact: 她也生 Mark 的气：气他死，更气他（在死之前就）离开；也气自己假装能修好一切，实则一直忽视了他正在死去。
facts.anchor: I was mad at Mark, too. I was mad at him for dying, obviously, but more to the point, I was mad at him for leaving, even before he died. And I was mad at myself for acting like I could fix it when really I had ignored the fact that he was dying.

facts.fact: 她追问：死于 AIDS 到底意味着什么？他死于某一夜病重而无人能让他继续呼吸——他到底死于什么？没有能救他的人足够在乎他。她母亲也是。
facts.anchor: What does it even mean to die of AIDS? He died because one night he was really sick and no one could keep him breathing, so what did he really die of? No one who could help cared enough about him. Or my mother.

facts.fact: 哀悼是为了荣耀他们、纪念他们对你的意义、为「你要在没有他们的世界里活下去」举行仪式；可当一个人本不该死时，一切仪式都像空洞的消遣——除非你说：好吧，随它去，坏事总会发生。
facts.anchor: You mourn people to honor them, to honor what they meant to you, to make a ceremony of the fact that you’re going to have to keep going without them. But when someone dies who should still be alive, all that ceremony feels like an empty fucking distraction—how can you ever, ever accept it without saying, Okay, sure, what can you do, bad things happen?

facts.fact: 那一刻握着球棒，她希望不要再见到 Mark——希望他不要回到这个糟糕的地方。
facts.anchor: In that moment, with the bat in my hands, I hoped I wouldn’t see Mark again, I hoped that he wouldn’t come back to this awful place.
